title: August and the Garden
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a cartographer who once mapped the living realms and now hides her gift behind a stall of harmless charms, learns that the crown's new witch-hunt is no purge at all: the king is harvesting gifted people to seal the failing border between realms with their memories. When Hazel's oldest friend is taken, she flees into the unmapped wilds with a runaway royal scribe, a fox-spirited child of the other realm, and an exiled hedge-witch who remembers the original covenant. To reforge it, Hazel must surrender her own treasured memories — including twelve years of found family — as the covenant's price. In the end she chooses to pay, but her companions refuse to let the price stand alone; each gives a memory in her stead, leaving Hazel whole but changed, and the realms bound not by sacrifice but by shared choice.
about_author: Oscar Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about what people carry when they cannot carry anything else, and live quietly with too many houseplants.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Stall
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. We meet Hazel selling charms that do nothing — or seem to — in the gray city of Vellmark, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering. A nervous young scribe, Wren, buys a compass charm that actually works, alarming them both. The emotional beat is quiet dread: Hazel has hidden for twelve years, and hiding is starting to feel like disappearing.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The crown proclaims a 'gifted census' — registration, they promise, nothing more. Hazel watches neighbors line up, then sees soldiers mark doors with ash sigils. That night, her old friend Tam, a gentle weather-worker, is dragged from his home. The beat is fear curdling into guilt: Hazel could have warned him and didn't.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a royal scribe, discovers the census ledgers hide a darker truth: the registered are shipped to the Sundered Marches and never return. Unable to unsee it, Wren defects, finding Hazel to confess what the crown intends — the king is feeding memories to the failing border. The beat is moral rupture and the first fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Out Through the Ash Gates
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Fleeing before dawn, Hazel and Wren rescue Tam's young daughter Sorrel — a fox-gifted child of the far realm smuggled over the border years ago. Pursued by the hunter-captain Ilsa Vane, they escape through a gate only Hazel can see. The beat is terror transformed into purpose: running together instead of alone.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Beyond the border lies a wild realm where geography obeys memory rather than distance. Hazel's cartography gift awakens fully — she can draw paths into being. But drawing costs her recollections, small ones first: a face, a song. The beat is wonder shadowed by cost, the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch of Hollowfen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a village grown inside a drowned forest, they find Maren, the last signatory of the original covenant between realms. Maren reveals the truth: the covenant was never broken by the other realm — the human king broke it, trading others' memories for his own long reign. The beat is fury and reframing: the enemy was always on their side of the border.

chapters.title: Vane at the Ford
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Captain Vane corners them at a river crossing; Sorrel's fox-gift saves them, but Tam's daughter burns out part of her gift doing it, and Hazel trades a year of memories to redraw the ford and drown the pursuit. The beat is grief and escalation — the price of survival is now being paid in front of everyone.

chapters.title: The Covenant Stone
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At the Covenant Stone beneath the Sundering rift, Maren explains the reforging requires freely given memories from both realms — and warns Hazel that hers, the mapmaker's, must anchor it. Hazel privately resolves to give everything, erasing her found family to save strangers. The beat is terrible resolve disguised as calm.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the stone, Vane arrives not to kill but to kneel — she has seen what the king does with the harvested. As Hazel begins the rite, offering all twelve years, Wren, Sorrel, Maren, and even Vane each press a hand to the stone and give memories of their own instead. The covenant takes from all and consumes none wholly. The beat is the climax: love refusing a lone sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Map With Room in It
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The border heals into something permeable and tended rather than sealed. Each companion carries small absences — a birthday, a lullaby — and chooses to fill them with new things together. Hazel opens a school of mapping in Hollowfen, teaching children of both realms. The final beat is bittersweet peace: memory fades, but family is remade daily, by choice.
